articles.title_orig: Trump arrives in China for a meeting with historic adversaries
articles.title_zh: Trump arrives in China for a meeting with historic adversaries
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
SHENZHEN, China — President Trump has begun an extraordinary visit to Shenzhen, where he is set to join the leaders of Russia and China — two of Washington’s principal geopolitical rivals — for an unprecedented trilateral summit on Thursday.
Chinese President Xi Jinping personally welcomed Trump on the tarmac upon his arrival, reciprocating a rare honor Trump extended to him during his September visit to Washington.
All three leaders attended a dinner alongside other regional heads of government on Wednesday night, participating in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, known as APEC.
The trilateral meeting will be the first of its kind held by leaders of the United States, Russia and China, three nations with the world’s largest nuclear arsenals.
But while Trump has embraced a strategy of diplomatic engagement with historic foes, the three leaders enter the meeting with starkly different agendas.
Russian President Vladimir Putin hopes to secure space and time to continue executing his war against Ukraine. Trump says he would like to discuss a nuclear arms control agreement and his war in Iran. And Xi aims to present China as a superpower on the international stage, capable of forging world peace.
Meeting with Putin before Trump arrived, Xi said that China’s relationship with Russia had remained as steadfast “as a rock through wind and rain.”
The two sides, he said, would pursue a “multipolar world” — a vision for a global balance of power that would see American influence weakened across Europe and Asia.
Trump, for his part, has hedged on his expectations of the summit, signaling resolve against China ahead of his arrival here.
On Monday, the Trump administration tightened export controls on semiconductor chips essential to AI development, closing loopholes aimed at curbing Chinese efforts to circumvent restrictions — a move that Trump himself acknowledged might “insult” Xi ahead of the meeting.
Chinese officials said on Wednesday afternoon that Beijing reserved the right to retaliate.
“In essence, the United States is simultaneously trying to find limited avenues of cooperation with China while trying to clamp down on their access to critical parts of the AI supply chain, which doesn’t set up the conditions for productive dialogue,” said Aalok Mehta, director of the Wadhwani AI Center at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
Trump also met in Manila on Tuesday with fellow members of the Quad — India, Japan and Australia — in a show of resolve toward Beijing.
“Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific,” Trump said in the Philippines.
“We continue to protect peace through strength,” he added.

articles.title_orig: Trump personally greeted by President Xi upon arrival in China
articles.title_zh: Trump personally greeted by President Xi upon arrival in China
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday morning ahead of historic trilateral talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.
Xi earlier welcomed President Donald Trump on the tarmac, which he said was a sign of reciprocity after Trump personally greeted him at the airport during a visit to the U.S. in September.
Trump is attending a welcome banquet alongside Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.
Trump is in China for the APEC summit, which President Xi opened with calls for free trade and greater cooperation around artificial intelligence. Highly anticipated talks with Xi and Putin are set for Thursday.
Xi said Thursday's leaders' meeting would discuss "measures to expand mutual openness, explore paths for innovation-driven growth, and broaden practical cooperation in various fields," according to Chinese state media. The Chinese president told Trump he wanted to "advance a constructive, strategic and stable relationship between China and the US based on respect, fairness and reciprocity," according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua. Trump said he was confident the visit would advance bilateral relations and prove successful, Xinhua reported.
Xi said: "We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition."
Putin has also addressed the summit , saying sanctions imposed on Russia have backfired and strengthened his nation.
The much-anticipated meeting between the three world leaders is set to take place on Thursday, with discussions expected to center on the Iran war and Russia's war in Ukraine.
Though expectations for any concrete outcome are low, Trump, Xi and Putin are expected to hold in-depth discussions on issues crucial for world peace and strategic stability, a spokesperson for China's foreign ministry said Monday.
North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un could attend the summit, which is a forum of 21 APEC member economies.
Trump flew in from Manila, Philippines, where he started a three-day visit to Asia and met key regional allies including Japan, India and Australia.
The APEC host city Shenzhen has been dubbed one of China's "Silicon Valleys" and has been a major hub for China's internet and artificial intelligence companies.
Beijing will position itself against what it calls "unilateralism and protectionism," with trade, artificial intelligence, and the Middle East expected to dominate the meeting's agenda.
Xi held several bilateral meetings with leaders on the sidelines Wednesday, including South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, with whom he discussed trade and commerce. Seoul's readout of the meeting also said the pair discussed peace on the Korean Peninsula, but this was omitted from Beijing's record of the talks.
The Chinese leader also met Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Vietnamese President To Lam earlier in the week.
Xi met with Putin earlier Wednesday, before Trump's arrival. The Chinese president called for greater cooperation between the two countries and spoke of providing a more stable and predictable business environment, according to Chinese state media, while promoting a "multipolar world and democratization of international relations."
Putin said Russia was looking to expand cooperation in trade, energy and education. The reports did not address Russia's war in Ukraine or the Iran war.
Trump will also hold bilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, amid hopes the pair can secure a lasting trade truce beyond January 2027. The meeting comes as the U.S. seeks to curb exports of artificial intelligence chips and amid concerns that Nvidia chips may have been diverted to China.

articles.title_orig: Apple restores services after internal update caused outages
articles.title_zh: Apple restores services after internal update caused outages
articles.content_orig:
Apple said it has restored all services after users reported issues with Apple Pay, Apple Support, iCloud and other products on Tuesday.
A spokesperson for the company told CBS News in an email that its services are "green across the board," referring to the System Status page on Apple's website, as of approximately 5:46 p.m. ET.
Thousands of people reported issues with Apple services on Tuesday, according to the tracking site Downdetector.com . The reports started to spike before noon ET and lasted several hours before tapering off in the afternoon, the site shows.
By 4:45 p.m. ET, Apple's system status page showed problems with iCloud sign-in and "AppleCare on device" had been resolved. However, some services, including Apple Business and Apple School Manager, were still experiencing issues, according to the tech giant.
The issues were not the result of a cyberattack, according to the spokesperson.
Apple is the latest company to experience service disruptions following a string of outages that affected everything from air travel to Microsoft email. On Monday, customers at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and other major financial institutions also reported service issues affecting bank deposits and Zelle transfers.
Users also reported issues accessing Gmail on Tuesday. In a statement shared on X, Google said it isn't "currently seeing evidence of a broad Gmail service disruption" and encouraged users to check its workplace status dashboard for updates.

articles.title_orig: Trump is greeted by Xi Jinping and meets with Canada’s Mark Carney as the China leg of his Asia trip gets underway
articles.title_zh: Trump is greeted by Xi Jinping and meets with Canada’s Mark Carney as the China leg of his Asia trip gets underway
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump greets as China's President Xi Jinping welcomes him after Trump steps off Air Force One at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen in southern China's Guangdong Province, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Mark Schiefelbein/AP hide caption
SHENZHEN, China — President Donald Trump landed in China on Wednesday, seeking to reinforce the U.S. status as the world's leading technology power, but a distressing series of technical outages back home has left the administration scrambling to calm the American public.
The issues put the administration on the defensive at a moment when the president wants to project strength and certainty ahead of a potentially complicated trilateral meeting on Thursday with the presidents of China and Russia, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
As he began his trip to Asia, Trump initially had been nonchalant about the outages that left people in the United States worried about accessing their email, checking their bank accounts or safely flying on an airplane.
"It's fine," Trump pronounced on Tuesday from the Philippine capital of Manila, suggesting it was all just a consequence of being a nation that is "big and powerful."
But then the outages involving Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, JPMorgan Chase and the National Security Agency's communications network began to overshadow Trump's visit. They raised the specter that artificial intelligence can disrupt daily life, as new cyber vulnerabilities identified require software to be constantly upgraded to fix flaws or other security holes, known as patching, which is supposed to improve how the technology runs.
So at the start of the second day of Trump's trip, Secretary of State Marco Rubio stepped in to reassure Americans on Trump's behalf. He told reporters there was "zero" evidence that the outages are connected or tied to rival nations, cyber hackers or criminals.
"Sometimes when you are going in to fix your system because you've identified a vulnerability, it creates a short-term disruption," said Rubio, who is also Trump's national security adviser.
Xi paid Trump a special honor by greeting him on the tarmac after Air Force One arrived in Shenzhen, China, reciprocating a gesture made by the U.S. president during Xi's state visit to Washington in September.
The two leaders greeted each other at the foot of the airplane's stairs in a handshake that became a hug as group of dancers waved flowers and flags. When Putin arrived earlier on Wednesday, Xi did not greet him at the airport despite their longstanding friendship.
Trump has signaled that he wants to take an improvised approach during his time in Shenzhen, the skyscraper-filled tech hub that is hosting world leaders for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It's a bet that his unscripted brand of diplomacy based on personal relationships can create some kind of legacy to reshape world affairs during his final two years in the White House.
On Thursday, at a first-ever trilateral, Trump said he plans to talk with Xi and Putin about limiting nuclear weapons and bringing an end to the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 with Russia's invasion. Analysts are not expecting substantive breakthroughs, despite the unprecedented nature of the meeting.
Before the trip, Trump's aides had told reporters that the war in Ukraine would not be on the agenda. But Trump said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict.
"I think it's very close to getting it done," Trump said. "We're going to have a good meeting on that."
Trump also teased the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate sit-down with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Rubio clarified on Wednesday that Trump was "serious" about meeting with Kim as a way of resolving tensions with North Korea. But he suggested no meeting was currently scheduled between Trump and Kim for Thursday.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., left, walks beside U.S. President Donald Trump during a welcome ceremony marking Trump's state visit to the Philippines at Malacanang Palace in Manila, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Aaron Favila/AP hide caption
Before he landed in Shenzhen, Trump had lunch in Manila with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at the Malacañang Presidential Palace.
Marcos noted that he had sent fried chicken from the Philippine chain Jollibee to the U.S. delegation for a late-night snack Tuesday and complimented Trump for "working very hard."
Trump praised the U.S. bond with the Philippines and the interior decoration of the presidential palace.
"Our people share common history, common values, common interests, common architectural tastes," Trump said. "I love what you've done here."
He said after their meeting that the two nations had reached a trade deal on Wednesday, though he had also said last year that an agreement had been reached. The U.S. trade deficit in goods with the Philippines has risen under Trump, climbing from $4.9 billion in 2024 to $12.8 billion during the first 9 months of this year, according to the Census Bureau.
There were no details about the new agreement, although the White House said it will involve Manila buying more energy and farm products.
Trump also had a short reunion with Imelda Marcos, the former first lady and mother of the Philippines' current president.
Famed for her lavish shoe collection, Imelda Marcos knew Trump decades ago through the New York City party scene. During the 1986 "People Power" uprising, her husband, Ferdinand Marcos, was ousted as the Philippines' strongman leader.
Trump called her "always the most beautiful" and the 97-year-old matriarch appeared to hand him a gift, according to a video posted by the White House.
Russian President Vladimir Putin speaks at the APEC CEO summit held ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, southern China's Guangdong province on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Dmitry Azarov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin hide caption
The prospect of Trump meeting with two of America's largest geopolitical rivals has been a source of unease as the U.S. president has been less welcoming of historic allies such as Canada and NATO partners in Europe.
His tariffs that were intended to curb China's trade surplus have done little to stop the progress of the world's dominant manufacturer, which for the second straight year will have exported $1 trillion more in goods than what it imported.
Even without the digital outages in the U.S., questions about how to handle AI loom over the summit.
The technology is viewed as key to unlocking faster economic growth, but its rapid development has meant it poses national security risks and could evolve in ways that put AI beyond human control.
Trump's close tech industry ally Jensen Huang was recently removed as the CEO of Nvidia after he admitted to an affair with a woman alleged to be an agent of the Chinese government. Beijing has denied that she was a spy, yet the affair raised concerns about how China has been able to access Nvidia computer chips to develop its own AI models that are competing with the U.S.
When asked this week why the U.S. had not been more aggressive in cutting off China's access to advanced computer chips, Trump said there were differences of opinion inside his administration and that "We have a very good relationship with China, and you don't want to insult them."
Trump has said he does not plan to bring up Taiwan, a self-governing island that China claims as its own. Taiwan is the leading manufacturer of advanced computer chips, including those designed by U.S. companies.
Still, Trump expects that Xi will push him on Taiwan's sovereignty.
"I'm sure he'll raise it," Trump said. "I won't have to raise it."

articles.title_orig: Nasdaq futures rise as Nvidia gains on earnings beat and solid outlook: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Nasdaq futures rise as Nvidia gains on earnings beat and solid outlook: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Analysts expect uncertainty around Nvidia 's future to linger despite another earnings beat, noting that much of the third quarter was already locked in before the turmoil that peaked in Jensen Huang 's resignation as CEO.
Nvidia's third-quarter revenue came in at $115.84 billion, more than $6 billion above analysts' expectations of $109.10 billion, while fourth-quarter guidance of $130 billion topped the $125.1 billion consensus, according to LSEG.
Part of that increase reflects an extra week in the fiscal fourth quarter, which Melius Research estimated accounts for $9 billion to $10 billion of the sequential jump.
The company also lifted its fiscal 2028 growth forecast to 75% from 70%, even with China excluded from its data center compute revenue outlook.
"That's a team going full steam ahead, rather than just steadying the ship, and a clear signal that management believes next year can run just fine without Jensen Huang at the helm," said Josh Gilbert, eToro's lead analyst for Asia Pacific and the Middle East.
Still, even with the results that he called "nothing short of astonishing", Gilbert said "investors will still be left with the uncertainty of who and what comes next."
In his first statement since he resigned last week, Huang said before the results release that he was open to returning to the company. However, chair of Nvidia's board Harvey Jones said on the earnings call that the board does not intend to reinstate him as CEO.
The results should help ease some concerns created by Nvidia's recent leadership turmoil, said Morningstar senior equity analyst Brian Colello, who described the figures as "solid" and broadly in line with the firm's expectations.
Colello expressed continued confidence that "the AI infrastructure buildout is real," pointing to Nvidia's shipments holding steady in the third quarter.
Michael Wilson, chief investment officer and chief U.S. equity strategist at Morgan Stanley, told CNBC TV that the results were "somewhat expected," with no major drop-off in Nvidia's business anticipated in the near term and guidance remaining "pretty constructive."
Wilson said AI remained a "desirable investment," with no slowdown in spending seen or expected from hyperscalers and some neoclouds — newer cloud providers built around AI computing. However, he added that investment may not continue at the pace investors expected six months ago.
Nvidia is widely seen as the bellwether for the broader AI industry and spending.
Gilbert shared that view, saying the AI trade can now "let out a small sigh of relief" after holding its breath for weeks. Nvidia had been "firing on all cylinders" before Huang's departure, he said, and its underlying fundamentals remained intact.
He pointed to Nvidia's supply commitments, which rose to $390 billion from $279 billion in three months, as well as its Vera Rubin platform, which has already brought in $20 billion.
"It's the clearest sign yet that the AI boom still has plenty of fuel in the tank," Gilbert said.
Nvidia shares rose more than 5% in after-hours trading, though Gilbert said any rally is expected to meet resistance and "plenty of volatility" in the coming weeks, with the CEO search only just getting under way and investigations still playing out.
New U.S. export restrictions announced this week add another wrinkle. The Commerce Department will require licenses for shipments of advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil, citing the risk that they could be diverted to China.
Gilbert said the direct impact on Nvidia's forecasts appears limited because its guidance already assumed no China data center revenue, while China accounted for only around 2% of sales this quarter. However, new licensing requirements for shipments to places such as Singapore and Malaysia could slow some neocloud build-outs, he said.
Melius Research analyst Ben Reitzes said fiscal 2028 is when sales to countries covered by the new restrictions would be expected to decline. He interpreted Nvidia's forecast as a sign that hyperscalers will take whatever supply becomes available elsewhere.
Nvidia said it is still studying the new Commerce Department rules but remains confident in its 75% growth target.
Colello pointed to longer-term risks around policy, international sales and hyperscalers developing their own chips, though he said Nvidia should remain an important player as the market expands.
He said investors will now be looking for the company to reaffirm its long-term outlook and show it can continue executing through the leadership transition.
"We're at a point of peak uncertainty because investors still don't know what Nvidia's long-term leadership will look like," Colello added.
"Jensen Huang's departure could create some near-term disruption, but a credible succession plan should go a long way toward steadying the ship. The next CEO will have big shoes to fill, but Nvidia's long-term opportunity does not hinge on one person."

articles.title_orig: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is a cultural and economic earthquake. Brace yourself.
articles.title_zh: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is a cultural and economic earthquake. Brace yourself.
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto VI protagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, against the backdrop of the Miami-inspired Vice City. Rockstar Games hide caption
I want to tell you about the time I saw Bigfoot. I want to tell you about sitting in the rain on a city street in a muscle car and prepping to rob a bank while lightning split the sky between high-rise condo towers in the distance and the drum fill from In The Air Tonight played on the radio. I want to tell you about gunfights and fistfights, the perfect satire of radio commercials and how the sunrise looks over Ocean Beach. But more than any of that, I want to tell you about the time an alligator bit my mom.
It happened in the backyard of an abandoned house with a rotting inground pool. My mom, Mia Caminos (mother of Lucia Caminos, one of the two leads in Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI , probably the most highly anticipated video game sequel of all time), was thrilled by the pool. Standing there, amid the artfully rendered weeds and trash, she spread her arms and told me to use my imagination, to see her vision for this ruin of a house with its upmarket water feature, in a scabby neighborhood on the outskirts of Vice City. She speaks in tones of increasingly frantic desperation because she has already put money down on this house, sight unseen. All of her money, actually, in hopes of flipping it and selling it fast to keep her startup real estate business afloat.
Lucia begins her epic as a petty criminal. Rockstar Games hide caption
The pool is still half full of water. There's a dirty, sodden mattress floating in it. And as if this is the main thing standing between her and success, Mia is fixated on getting it out of the pool.
Help me, Lucia , she says.
And, dutifully, I do. Playing as Lucia, I grab hold, mash buttons, help my mom drag away the wet, heavy, stinking mattress. And just as we get it up and over the lip of the pool that's going to be the thing that makes this wreck of a house suddenly desirable – that's when the alligator lunges out of the murky water, grabs my mom by the arm and tries to drag her back in.
This is a story about folly, fixation, unrealistic expectations of success at the ass-end of late capitalism, and the vicious, whip-crack cruelty of predators who lie in wait for anyone trying to improve a terrible situation.
But then I shoot the alligator in the head before it can eat my mom. Because this is also a story about violence, and how sometimes (maybe all the times), the loud, cathartic rip of gunfire is the only solution left for people who have already lost so much and can't bear to see one more thing taken from them.
It's a story about my mom and an alligator, sure.
It is also the story of GTA6
Grand Theft Auto VI returns to Vice City and its Florida-inspired environs. Rockstar Games hide caption
But let's back up a little. For anyone who has somehow missed the shrieking, neon-and-swamp-water marketing onslaught over the past several days, weeks, months and years, Grand Theft Auto VI is the newest release from Rockstar Games. It is a Bonnie and Clyde love story, a knife-edged satire of modern American culture and politics, an unapologetic murder simulator, a love letter to 50 years of crime movies, and a thoughtful, emotional meditation on the sacrifices, small and large, that we make for family. A massive open world game set in the fictional state of Leonida (based on the very real state of Florida), it represents a return to a location that Rockstar hasn't visited in-depth since its 2002 release of GTA: Vice City , and is the first new game in the franchise since GTA5 launched in 2013. According to estimates, it already earned over $1.5 billion in pre-sales and will likely make a total of $3 to $5 billion in its first week , which could make it the largest single entertainment product launch ever.
Fans have been waiting years for it. They have created libraries worth of lore and theories and dissected trailers frame-by-frame. To discount the overheated environment into which this singular work of art is being released would be doing a disservice both to it and the legions of salivating prognosticators who have made guessing the number of bird species included in-game , or speculating on the square mileage of its map, their entire personalities.
While Vice City remains the game's hub, most of its map is actually rural or wild. Rockstar Games hide caption
Now, though, they know it all. We all do. We know that GTA6 is expansive, covering everything from the Keys (where the game starts) to the hilly, forested north, with Vice City in all its grimy, pastel-colored splendor at the beating heart of it. It is a playground, equal parts gorgeous and maniacal, and in all that space the developers have given us a thousand different things to do. You can rob a bank or take a bike ride, go fishing, hunt trophy animals, visit strip clubs, rob random civilians, street race, fly drones, eat a sandwich, work out, manage your family savings account, jump a sports car off the top of a building, steal a plane, punch out a convenience store clerk, fight a bear or, yes, just wander out toward the horizon and study the birds. And while some of that is fun and all of it is diverting (at least for a little while), none of it is the ostensible point. The game-y part of the game — the hundred extras and time-wasters that players have come to expect from open-world projects in general, and GTA specifically — is not what makes it matter.
What matters is Mia and the alligator, Lucia and the gun. It's the multi-pronged, exquisitely balanced narrative about poverty and rigged systems that makes it hard to turn away from GTA while you're playing and impossible not to think about when you're away.
Jason and his pal, Cal, shoot pool. Rockstar Games hide caption
Lucia is an ex-con, a car thief and a small-time criminal who got caught trying to rob a payday loan joint and starts the game in jail. Her partner, Jason Duval, is a veteran, dishonorably discharged, now making a living flying loads for a local coke dealer down in the Keys and living rent-free in one of his properties. Jason skims a little on the coke deals, wears flip-flops and drinks beer in the sun, and goes fishing with his best friend Cal (played with genius-level goofy, drunken paranoia and dopey bravado by Bobby Moynihan). Jason and Lucia have a kid, Tomás, who is currently living with Lucia's family, and every plan they have is about getting right by the law, making a few bucks and grabbing a chance at finally being a family.
Only there are complications — surprisingly banal ones at first (like not being able to open a checking account because of their bad credit) — that slowly ramp up into huge ones across 60-odd hours of main story gameplay that see Jason and Lucia (both of whom are playable characters) graduate from knocking over liquor stores in a beat-up El Camino, to pulling off elaborate heists in the middle of Vice City which will have you dangling from a net suspended from a cargo helicopter hauling 200 tons of cocaine. It goes from Badlands to Die Hard with the speed of a muscle car, all bright chrome and barking straight pipes. From True Romance to Heat like that's just the natural arc of any American love story.
And what's remarkable about the whole bloody delight is that it remains, until its final operatic moments, so surprisingly grounded. This is a somewhat more mature GTA than its predecessors, trading aliens, cannibal cultists and whacked-out drug trips for wellness influencers, local politics and the music industry. Jason and Lucia's relationship is the superstructure around which the entire narrative is built, and it's a dynamic thing that must be maintained in a dozen little ways — making coffee in the morning, opening doors for each other, date nights (even if that means robbing a jewelry store together), or holding hands as you walk toward yet another betrayal by someone you thought you could trust. articles.content_orig:
Plus, high-stake negotiations are underway at the United Nations over killer robots, Palantir’s CEO is trying to rebrand his company as “progressive” and more — all in this week’s Tuesday Tech Drop.
Happy Tuesday! Here’s your Tuesday Tech Drop, some of the past week’s top stories from the intersection of politics and technology.
According to a new report from Reuters, the value of President Donald Trump ’s meme coin has cratered to record lows ahead of a cryptocurrency gala this weekend at his South Florida estate. The report also says that interest in the president’s third such gala “has collapsed.”
Rep. Robert Garcia, a California Democrat who is primed to become chair of the House Oversight Committee in January, told MS NOW that looking at Trump’s crypto ventures — and investors who may have felt legitimately scammed — will be a priority for his committee.
A federal judge has issued a permanent injunction barring the Justice Department or Department of Homeland Security from pressuring Apple to suppress Eyes Up, an app used for documenting immigration enforcement activity.
Read more at the Indiana Capital Chronicle .
As Trump continues to voice support for Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO amid a scandal involving his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, scrutiny continues to mount over the president’s financial stake in the company behind some of the world’s most-coveted computer chips . My colleague Steve Benen wrote about recent reports on the timing and frequency with which Trump has traded Nvidia stock that raise even more questions.
High-stakes negotiations are underway at the United Nations as representatives gather this week to discuss potential regulations on lethal autonomous weapons.
Palantir CEO Alex Karp, whose tech firm has been central to Trump’s racist anti-immigrant crackdown , is trying to rebrand his company as “progressive” after Democrats’ blue wave in the midterms.
Trump has invested in several of the companies that his transportation secretary wants to build a multibillion-dollar network for the Federal Aviation Administration after last week’s nationwide ground stop debacle, and I wrote about the president’s financial entanglements.
An Army major and whistleblower said Pentagon leaders shrugged off warnings about the need for adequate protection before an Iranian drone strike killed six U.S. service members. Trump responded by raging at CBS News’ “60 Minutes” for airing the claims — without disputing their merits.

articles.title_orig: Wall Street prepares for Anthropic IPO frenzy, despite broader AI stock slump
articles.title_zh: Wall Street prepares for Anthropic IPO frenzy, despite broader AI stock slump
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic is likely to price its IPO above the current range of $70 to $78, multiple sources told CNBC's David Faber on Tuesday.
The artificial intelligence company is planning to close the order books and lock in total demand at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. Anthropic is slated to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" and start trading on Nov. 19.
If Anthropic's IPO proceeds as planned, the company will debut roughly five months after SpaceX went public in a record offering that raised $85.7 billion. But Anthropic is facing a public market that's grown increasingly skeptical of the AI trade, as well as mounting and widespread antipathy toward the technology in the U.S.
A group of researchers, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei , co-founded the company in 2021 after defecting from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude , and it underwent a period of explosive growth in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of its AI coding tool, Claude Code .
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, Anthropic said it generated $33.24 billion in revenue, up roughly 1,200% from the same period last year, according to its prospectus . It reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Anthropic lost $25.1 billion over the same stretch in 2025, the filing said.
Anthropic has long worked to establish a reputation as a safety-conscious AI company, and its prospectus included more than 90 pages of risk factors for investors to consider ahead of its listing.
"I think if we do this right, we can create an age of miracles where humanity is able to solve problems that have eluded us for millennia," Amodei said in Anthropic's roadshow video . "We have to make sure that all the risks, all the ways that things can go wrong with this technology, we very carefully address those risks as we bring the benefits and as we have a viable business at the same time."
"I invite you to join us on the next phase of this journey," Amodei said.

articles.title_orig: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.title_zh: In Choosing Shenzhen for Trump-Putin Summit, Xi Shows Off His Tech Ambitions
articles.content_orig:
Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy
I n a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping , is basking in its neon glow.
On the sidelines, a series of high-profile bilateral meetings and the announcement of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have cemented Xi’s status as an agenda setter on the global stage.
The broader Apec summit , meanwhile, provides an opportunity for China to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms “unilateralism and protectionism” – that is to say, trade measures taken against Beijing by countries such as the US.
All this is set against the futuristic backdrop that is Shenzhen, a city that perhaps better than no other embodies China’s rise into a confident, technologically innovative power central to the global economy.
A photo display in the Apec media centre charts Shenzhen’s transformation from sparsely populated marshland, calling it “a miracle in the history of world development created by the Chinese people”.
“[Xi] wants people to go home Chinamaxxing,” said Prof Astrid Nordin, of King’s College London. “Shenzhen is itself part of the message. It’s a showcase of Chinese technological and economic achievements, and of China’s claim that it offers opportunities for prosperity in a world increasingly characterised by uncertainty and conflict.”
Like the light show, the summit is being carefully coordinated. The Financial Times cited people familiar with the matter as saying it would be one of the most tightly controlled in the organisation’s history, with leaders having to travel to a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park to meet Xi. The paper said diplomats had grumbled that the format “seems designed to reduce the free-flowing discussion characteristic of prior editions”.
Setting out its expectations for the summit, China’s foreign ministry has said it looks forward to “practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on”.
Already, Xi has announced trade wins with Canada’s Mark Carney, extending remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.
A meeting with Papua New ⁠Guinea’s leader, meanwhile, showed how Beijing’s geopolitical priorities have been absorbed and reflected by its allies, with James Marape recounting to Xi how he had closed Taiwan’s office in his country despite domestic challenges in doing so.
The most important meeting will be between Xi and Trump. The leaders of the world’s two superpowers are expected to tackle a broad range of issues including AI and trade. In a move that could strain the fragile tariff truce that the two leaders first agreed last year, the Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.
Christopher Adams, a senior adviser at the law firm Covington who was at the centre of trade negotiations with China for the Obama and first Trump administrations, said: “The trade truce may increasingly look like a ceasefire in a war where major combat operations remain on hold but skirmishes are escalating to the point where the line between peace and war is blurred.
“I don’t see pressure to announce a further extension of the trade truce in Shenzhen. If a significant extension is announced, that would be an upside surprise.”
China has not hesitated to leverage Apec’s multinational platform in service of its arguments. A commentary by the state news agency Xinhua on Tuesday said: “Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, [China’s hosting] sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country’s development need not come at the expense of another.”
The chair of the Apec senior officials’ meeting, Chen Xu, said Beijing had made trade “openness” a key focus of its Apec year and looked forward to “achieving more practical outcomes on the trade front”.
The much anticipated trilateral summit with Trump and Putin, on the other hand, could prove largely symbolic. For Xi, “it provides the appearance of China shaping the world order as an equal to the United States,” said Dr Kevork Oskanian, an expert on Russia at the University of Exeter. “Agreement on substantial issues, which would, in any case, require extensive preparatory negotiations, is unlikely.”
For China’s ruling Communist party, the political pomp has another key purpose. Nordin said summits were “occasions for leaders to tell stories about the world, about their country’s place in it … and one of the most important audiences for those stories is at home.”
For the locals watching the skyscraper light show on Monday night, the symbolism was not lost. China’s export might had helped it become increasingly powerful on the world stage, said one local man, who did not give his name. “It’s so great that the summit will take place in Shenzhen,” he said. “I feel very proud.”

articles.title_orig: 2028 Ford Mustang GTD Gets A Special Edition 125 Years In The Making
articles.title_zh: 2028 Ford Mustang GTD Gets A Special Edition 125 Years In The Making
articles.content_orig:
The Ford Mustang GTD is getting a few small tweaks for 2028. The automaker’s ultimate Pony Car gets a new special edition that celebrates "Sweepstakes"—the car Henry Ford built and raced in 1901 as a last-ditch effort to attract investors.
Ford won, and 125 years later, the Blue Oval is honoring that special car with a unique livery for the Mustang GTD. The new 1901 livery replaces last year's Spirit of America package and features Royal Red exterior paint with black accents. The splitter, diffuser, rockers, and rear wing feature exposed carbon fiber.
Inside, the 1901 livery comes with mahogany red leather seats and race red stitching. The Performance Package , which includes aerodynamic updates and a weight reduction, is standard.
2028 Ford Mustang GTD 1901
Beyond the new livery, the 2028 Mustang GTD gets redesigned 3D-printed titanium paddle shifters and a new shift ring. Full-grain leather now wraps around the center console, the door panels, and the instrument panel.
Optional magnesium wheels will also be available for the 2028 model year. Ford introduced them with the car's launch but has faced supplier constraints, which the automaker says have been resolved.
On the outside, Ford has new painted stripe options. There’s also an updated livery for the Liquid Carbon with teal accents and striping. Incognito Green and Teal Tonic exterior colors have been added, replacing Sage Green and Blue Metallic.
Ford didn’t touch the powertrain. Under the hood is Ford’s supercharged 5.2-liter V8 engine, with its dry-sump oil system. It still makes 815 horsepower and 664 pound-feet of torque, with a rear-mounted eight-speed dual-clutch transaxle.
The top speed remains 202 miles per hour, and Brembo ceramic brakes provide the stopping power for the Mustang . Ford will release pricing information closer to the Mustang’s on-sale date.
Interested buyers can begin placing orders in December, with deliveries expected to start in the second quarter of 2027.

articles.title_orig: Grand Theft Auto VI Uses AMD FSR 4 On Xbox Series S, Upscaling 720p To 1080p While Still Running Ray Traced Global Illumination
articles.title_zh: Grand Theft Auto VI Uses AMD FSR 4 On Xbox Series S, Upscaling 720p To 1080p While Still Running Ray Traced Global Illumination
articles.content_orig:
During Grand Theft Auto VI 's review period , Rockstar Games offered us the chance to send some questions to the developers. Being a tech-focused website, there was a lot we wanted to know about the studio's design goals for this iteration of the RAGE engine .
Did they try to achieve a frame rate higher than 30 frames per second ? What were the rendering resolutions for each system? What kind of challenges did adding ray traced global illumination present, and what was their approach to HDR support?
All of these questions are answered below in a lengthy statement crafted by Jonathon Ashcroft - Senior Vice President of Technology, Chris Oat – Technical Director: Engine and Graphics, and Marc Chambers – Technology Production Director.
It became clear early on that given the scale of the team’s ambition, we’d be targeting 30fps on this generation of hardware. We’ve put a lot of effort into balancing presentation, simulation, and gameplay, as well as ensuring the input latency is vastly improved vs. Grand Theft Auto V and Red Dead Redemption 2. Part of that process was determining our base resolution and upscaling solution. We evaluated a variety of approaches for each console, then selected a combination of each that gave us the look and performance we needed.
On all platforms, the picture is then composited with a 4K UI and presented. For each console, we’ve arrived at our solution through careful evaluation of both the visuals and the performance.  We built our core lighting, frame processing, and final presentation pipeline with both HDR and SDR support in mind from the outset. We calibrated our engine’s in-game light sources according to the real-world physical properties of natural and artificial light sources.
We also built a new physically-based material library used to represent every material type you will see in game. From the way muddy alligator skin glistens in the Leonida sunshine, to the way hair and clothing reacts to the dynamic light shows in a nightclub, and the complex lighting interactions of exotic vehicle paint zipping under highway street lights — it was all built to behave according the physical laws of light. Finally, that rendered frame goes through an imaging pipeline modelled after real word cinematic camera and film treatment, much like you would expect of a modern movie. The aim is always to try and create and preserve emersion for the player, so they can experience it as the team imagined it, whether they are experiencing the game in HDR or SDR.
This focus on lighting made it vital for us to ensure we could use the same lighting solution on each console, including the Xbox Series S, where memory pressure posed a bit of a challenge. The results made that a challenge worth overcoming. There are indeed some differences between the implementations per console, as we rebalance the RTGI features to achieve the best presentation based on each platform’s capabilities. As with everything, we tune on a given piece of hardware to achieve the presentation we’re looking for, so there’s no single solution.
I also asked Rockstar a couple of more artistic questions, which were answered separately by the studio's VP of Art, Michael Kane . You can find them below.
The game's corners of the screen often seem a little darkened, kind of like a vignette effect. Can you confirm that's the case? If so, would it be possible to add it as a toggle option for those who dislike it?
Michael Kane, Vice President of Art: Dynamic: The vignette effect is an artistic choice. We currently do not support any toggle, but we have recently identified and fixed an issue where it was becoming stronger than intended in certain circumstances.
In key Grand Theft Auto VI artworks, Jason looks very different from the in-game character, whereas Lucia looks much closer. How did your design for each character evolve through development, and did you have any specific references or inspirations that you can share?
Michael Kane, Vice President of Art: Dynamic: There could typically be a perceptual interpretation of the key art versus in-game, especially for Jason… because both of them are so customizable, we think many players will maybe want ‘their Jason’ to have a mustache or long hair in a certain style or colour etc when they play. So far, we’ve only seen those more diverse looks on him in screenshots and not key marketing art, so that’s the best anchor point for our intention for him – that’s his ground truth, in-game.
About the author : With over two decades of experience in gaming journalism, Alessio Palumbo has led the gaming vertical at Wccftech since August 2015. He started working at a young age for Italian websites like Everyeye.it, Gamestar.it, Nextgame.it, and Multiplayer.it before kickstarting the indie English-language publication Worlds Factory as its founder and Editor in Chief. 

In the last decade, he has coordinated the overall output of Wccftech's gaming section, managed PR relations, assigned reviews, produced daily news coverage, edited gaming content as needed, and delivered game reviews.  

Arguably, his trademark content is the long series of exclusive developer interviews that have been cited by Wikipedia and by the biggest news media and gaming publications. 

His passion for technology also makes him knowledgeable when it comes to gaming hardware and tech. His favorite genres include RPGs, MMORPGs, and action/adventure games.

articles.title_orig: Rubio says there's "zero evidence" recent tech outages are related
articles.title_zh: Rubio says there's "zero evidence" recent tech outages are related
articles.content_orig:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there's "zero evidence" that recent tech outages in U.S. air travel, banking and other systems are connected.
"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA . The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said Wednesday morning local time during a news conference in the Philippines.
Rubio acknowledged that people are fearful and uncertain, saying he wanted to be clear that the United States is not under systemic attack.
"We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind," Rubio said.
Rubio, who is traveling with President Trump ahead of a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, added that the administration is "always on the lookout" for any potential attacks and reiterated multiple times that reports of technical issues are not interconnected.
"Each of them are distinct, and they're different in their causation," he said.
On Thursday, Microsoft said it experienced a worldwide outage affecting services like Outlook and Teams, impacting users, companies and government operations worldwide. The company said the outage was linked to a technical issue, not malicious or cyber activity.
The following day, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on all departing U.S. flights for several hours, throwing the aviation industry into turmoil. Federal officials identified a contractor performing maintenance updates as the cause of Friday's disruption, but key questions remain about the underlying cause of the systemwide failure.
Other recent outages that have since been resolved include disruptions to major banks like JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and U.S. Bank, and issues with Apple's services . On Tuesday, the National Security Agency 's internal network used to store and share classified information went offline, multiple U.S. officials familiar told CBS News.
Democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also said on Tuesday that there's no indication these incidents are the result of an attack, but noted that artificial intelligence is creating pressure for companies to deal with vulnerabilities.
"AI is making it possible to identify vulnerabilities across enormous numbers of systems at unprecedented speed, creating enormous pressure on companies and government agencies to patch those vulnerabilities immediately, often all at once, putting tremendous strain on systems that weren't built to handle that pace of change," Warner said in a post on X . "It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences.   This is exactly why I've been pushing for commonsense guardrails on AI and stronger cybersecurity protections."
When asked Wednesday about the role of AI in recent incidents, Rubio said he didn't want to speculate because every incident is unique and referred to individual companies.

articles.title_orig: Putin Arrives in Asia With a Show of Force: Nuclear Bombers
articles.title_zh: Putin Arrives in Asia With a Show of Force: Nuclear Bombers
articles.content_orig:
Japan says it launched fighter jets and "strongly" protested after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace early on Tuesday.
South Korea also says it deployed fighter jets, while Taiwan says it "responded" to Russian military aircraft detected in their respective air defence identification zones.
These are unofficial buffer areas beyond territorial airspace where governments identify approaching aircraft for security purposes. Moscow has yet to comment.
The alleged incursions are a reminder of Russia's military power ahead of the Apec economic summit in China this week, which Vladimir Putin will attend alongside US President Donald Trump.
Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said the flight paths of the Russian aircraft, off the south-western Okinoshima island, were a "serious infringement of Japan's sovereignty" and "completely unacceptable".
The last such incursion was in 2024, when a Russian military patrol plane entered Japanese airspace off Rebun island, Hokkaido.
Taiwan says its military "responded accordingly" after two Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone, also on Tuesday.
South Korea says it sent up jets after an unspecified number of Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone over the Sea of Japan. The aircraft departed without violating South Korean airspace, authorities said.
It is unclear if the three neighbours were responding to the same or different aircraft.
The East China Sea contains self-declared, overlapping air defence identification zones between China, Taiwan, Japan and South Korea.
Foreign military aircraft are expected, but not legally required, to notify governments before entering such air defence identification zones.
Tensions are flaring between Japan and Russia, which are locked in a decades-old territorial dispute over a cluster of islands in the Pacific Ocean.
For months, Moscow has been ratcheting up the pressure on Tokyo.
In August, Putin paid his first visit to one of these islands, prompting sharp rebuke from Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. In October, Russia detained a Japanese journalist on spying allegations.

articles.title_orig: 42 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's Black Friday eShop Sale (Europe)
articles.title_zh: 42 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's Black Friday eShop Sale (Europe)
articles.content_orig:
The once one-day event of 'Black Friday' seems to last for almost all of November these days. Anyway, Nintendo has kicked off its digital discounts with an eShop sale in Europe.
The EU Black Friday eShop sale is now live and will be sticking around until 29th November , offering big savings on a bunch of Switch 1 and 2 bangers.
We have assembled the following list to highlight the cream of the crop — who has time to scroll through thousands of games, after all. Below, you'll find every game in Nintendo's Black Friday sale that we awarded a 9/10 or higher. We've also added a personal pick at the end from the games that fall below that threshold, because we just couldn't resist.
Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube 855k
As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store .
Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.
13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim is a wonderful achievement for dynamic storytelling, as it puts forth a compelling and multifaceted narrative that’ll keep you guessing right up until the very end.
This excellent story, combined with enjoyable combat portions, a striking art style, and some top-notch voice acting make for an experience that you shouldn't miss. It’s the kind of game that’ll have you wishing that you could play it again for the first time, just so all its best elements could be new again.
Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown is the absolute pinnacle of the series and despite coming to Switch over five years after other platforms, this 'impossible' Switch conversion does very little to degrade the experience. Long-time franchise players and military aviation enthusiasts will be overwhelmed by the fan service at every turn, from craters on the ground to airplanes, liveries, callsigns, and emblems shouting out to previous entries.
We understand the genre is uniquely niche, but if this is your first foray into the franchise, this conversion is a perfect gateway into this rich, revered series. You get tons of content and an epic single-player campaign wrapped up in triple-A presentation that delivers the most comprehensive portable experience ever from Project Aces.
Aegis Defenders is a fantastic game, brilliantly blending the tower defence and platforming genres in a unique way to produce a memorable and enjoyable experience.
Lovable characters, interesting lore, plenty of secrets, engaging gameplay, and gorgeous presentation combine to make this a must-have for your Switch, a real gem on the eShop.
AI: The Somnium Files – nirvanA Initiative is one of the most interesting visual novels we’ve played through in a while. The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.
Even with some minor control issues, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.
Alwa’s Legacy is an excellent example of how to do a proper sequel; it takes everything that Alwa's Awakening did well and builds on it, adds in a few new ideas of its own, and corrects the issues that were previously present.
It may be a little on the short side, but Alwa’s Legacy is the special sort of game that only comes around once in a great while, reminding you of the kind of quality that’s possible when a dedicated crew puts in the time to make a polished and tightly designed final product.
While this turn-based affair might look, move, and feel just like a real board game, Armello is actually a completely original creation — and one that does more than simply doff its cap at the world of tabletop gaming. From the deep tactics of its living board game gameplay to the sheer charm of its worldbuilding and animal character designs, it's a quest filled with back-stabbing, political power plays, and rampaging monsters that’s different each and every time you play. It’s at its absolute best when played in multiplayer, that human factor making for an even more unpredictable battle for the corrupted throne. The Switch version has had its ups and downs since launch, with some updates making things worse, but it's apparently back to being in a playable state on Nintendo's console. As such, you’d be doing yourself a disservice not to add this anthropomorphic tale to your wishlist.
Astral Ascent is a prime example of a game that amounts to more than the sum of its parts. Its strong character design, hi-bit visuals, tight combat, memorable bosses, and broad build variety have all featured in games you’ve probably played before—there’s nothing ‘new’ here.
But to write it off as just 'another one of those' in a crowded genre would be to miss out on one of the most delightful and surprising releases of 2023. Astral Ascent is comfortably one of the best roguelites available on the Switch. Don't miss it.
Catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent new character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.
If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough new content here to make it worth diving in all over again.
An extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface issues which are easily ignored.
At roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.
It's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.
There isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.
Even so many years after its 2005 debut, Devil May Cry 3 remains one of the very best action games ever made. It may have aged in places, but that turbo-charged, combo-heavy action feels as fresh today as it did back in the mid-noughties.
The new Freestyle mode – which lets players swap combat styles on the fly at any point during the action – is a genuinely excellent addition to the package, and the ability to play Bloody Palace in local co-op is the cherry on top of a Switch port that should appeal to anyone interested in sampling the devilish delights of this all-time classic.
Dragon Ball FighterZ on the Switch is, simply put, one of the best fighting games we've seen on the system. Arc System Works went the extra mile in capturing the essence of the source material and distilled it into an incredible brawler that has lost nothing in the transition to Nintendo's hybrid console.
The stunning visuals, intense action, and easy-to-master controls make FighterZ a game all fans of the genre should have in their library. If you only play this kind of game casually, it remains a must-own.
Every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first plac

articles.title_orig: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
articles.title_zh: Steve Rosenberg: Historic talks with Xi and Trump are a coup for Putin
articles.content_orig:
The meeting hasn't even happened yet.
But Thursday's mini summit of Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping already looks like a win for the Kremlin.
Think back to 2022. After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine President Putin was an international pariah. Western leaders were determined to isolate him and his country over the war in Ukraine.
Fast forward to 2026: Vladimir Putin has secured an historic meeting in Shenzhen. For the first time in history, the leaders of China, Russia and the United States will sit down – just the three of them – for talks.
That puts Putin exactly where he wants to be: at the top table of global politics, rubbing shoulders with the leaders of the two great powers.
It allows him to boast that Western pressure on Russia has failed.
"We see such examples in the failed attempts to isolate our country, Russia, which has faced unprecedented sanctions pressure," Putin told a business forum of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation organisation.
That was followed by a meeting with Xi Jinping.
But the Kremlin says the "showstopper" event in Shenzhen will be Putin's trilateral with Xi and Trump.
It allows him to play global statesman, even as the Russian military continues to pound Ukrainian towns and cities, and the Kremlin continues to reject the idea of an unconditional, comprehensive ceasefire.
One short meeting is unlikely to reshape the world. But it's the optics that are key. The picture. The photo-op. Three leaders, three big powers, discussing big issues.
In a way, Vladimir Putin will use this meeting to send a holiday postcard to the rest of the world. Instead of "Wish you were here", he'll sign it: "Look: I'm here."
But what of those who are not at the table?
Among European leaders, and especially in Ukraine, there is concern that the three-way meeting might produce more than just a pretty picture, though not in a good way for Kyiv.
Donald Trump has already said that in Shenzhen he wants to discuss his "favourite subject" - the war in Ukraine. The Kremlin would likely welcome an opportunity to argue its case to Trump and Xi without Ukrainian officials or European leaders in the room.
Last month Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed concern that the Putin-Trump-Xi meeting might resemble the Yalta Conference of 1945. That is when the leaders of the Soviet Union, Britain and the United States – Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt - met to re-organise post-World War Two Europe.
"We really don't want this to turn into 'Yalta 2, 3, 4' with a redistribution of influence," said Zelensky.
It is unclear whether China would want the Ukraine war on the agenda in Shenzhen. In its official statements on the upcoming trilateral meeting, Beijing has talked more generally about the need to discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability".
In Shenzhen, Russia will make the most of the optics. But a diplomatic victory is not the same as a military one.
Nearly five years after President Putin launched his so-called "special military operation", Russia is still struggling to win its war on Ukraine.
Over this time, it has suffered huge losses on the battlefield.
And the Ukrainian strike on the road bridge linking Russia to the Crimean Peninsula – carried out on the eve of the summit - was a blow to Moscow's prestige. The attack severely damaged part of the multi-billion-dollar bridge built by Russia after it annexed Crimea from Ukraine.
The damage is not only a logistical headache for the Russian authorities.
It is a reminder that the Kremlin's "special operation" has not gone at all to plan.
The Shenzhen summit may give Vladimir Putin a big stage, and a bright spotlight.
It does not necessarily bring him closer to winning the war.

articles.title_orig: Russia, China should ‘lead’ push to multipolar world, Xi tells APEC summit
articles.title_zh: Russia, China should ‘lead’ push to multipolar world, Xi tells APEC summit
articles.content_orig:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has said that Beijing and Moscow should “lead and advance the trend towards a multipolar world” following a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit .
Xi and Putin held bilateral discussions on Wednesday in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.
Following Xi, Putin took to the stage, telling the summit that Western powers were “former hegemons”, adding that Europe was in the midst of a “humiliating decline”.
“Experience has shown that the traditional tools of economic dominance and de facto coercion have largely run their course, having lost much of their intimidating power,” Putin said.
“While sanctions, tariffs and export restrictions may still exert a certain deterrent effect, they are incapable of halting growth – let alone crushing the economies of competitors.”
Russia’s economy has been heavily sanctioned by the US and Europe because of its war against Ukraine, which began in February 2022 when Moscow invaded its neighbour.
Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Shenzhen, said that both Xi and Putin called for a “more fair and multipolar world order and that the two leaders also said they would maintain close ties amid what they both described as global uncertainty”.
She added that Xi and Putin “have a close personal relationship, and they have met more than 40 times over the years, and these two countries are also strategically aligned”, with China remaining Russia’s biggest trading partner, and Russia providing Beijing with much-needed energy resources.
“Putin clearly took a swing at European countries, in particular, that have put sanctions on Russia,” Yu added.
But in Shenzhen, “Putin is having a bit of a moment in the sun” at the APEC summit, where he is being treated as a guest of honour.
Robert Kelly, a professor of political science at Pusan National University in South Korea’s Busan, said that all three leaders are “coming in with fairly different expectations and desires of what they want”.
“That’s going to make it quite difficult for them to actually find an agreement,” he said. “Nuclear weapons is an area where the three leaders could really make some great progress,” he argued, adding that the current “tripolar world of nuclear powers is different than the Cold War”.
“It would be great if the three of them could actually bring [the arms race] under control,” Kelly told Al Jazeera.
“But all the different parties are in different places – for the Russians, their weapons are very important to bolster their perception as a great power, despite their problems in Ukraine,” he noted.
“The Chinese have engaged in a major buildup, and it doesn’t look like they want arms control, nuclear weapons at least in their 10 years; and the United States has been sort of very standoffish about any kind of deal,” Kelly said.
“There’s a very strong public goods argument for a positive outcome, for an arms control agreement, but it just won’t happen,” he added.
APEC was established in 1989 and has 21 members, accounting for more than 50 percent of global gross domestic product (GDP) and representing about 2.7 billion people.
The organisation aims to support economic growth and prosperity in the Asia Pacific region.
Leaders are expected to discuss a range of important issues at this year’s summit, including artificial intelligence (AI) and trade – two areas in which the US and China play dominant roles.
A key issue for APEC members and the wider world is the trade truce between Washington and Beijing, and whether it will be extended beyond January.

articles.title_orig: ADNOC Ship Attacked in Hormuz as Maritime Security Risks Rise
articles.title_zh: ADNOC Ship Attacked in Hormuz as Maritime Security Risks Rise
articles.content_orig:
ABU DHABI — ADNOC Logistics and Services confirmed on 18 November 2026 that one of its vessels was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of 17 November, leaving 1 crew member missing and 11 injured, according to statements reported by The National and Gulf News. Search and rescue operations are ongoing “in co-ordination with the relevant authorities,” the company said.
In a separate incident, the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT Tara Gas was struck and disabled approximately 7 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, on 16 November, leaving 1 Indian national missing and 2 hospitalised, according to India’s Ministry of External Affairs. A third vessel — the Panama-flagged crude tanker On Phoenix, which is UAE-owned — was also struck by an unknown projectile on 16 November, according to Riviera Maritime and gCaptain. The 3 attacks within roughly 24 hours added to an intensifying pattern of shipping violence in a waterway that has seen dozens of vessel damage incidents since the war began on 28 February 2026.
The House of Saud Daily Briefing
Saudi Arabia's news in 3 minutes, every morning. Free. See today's issue
✓ You're in. Your first briefing arrives tomorrow morning.
ADNOC Logistics and Services confirmed the attack occurred on the evening of 17 November 2026 but did not disclose the vessel’s name, hull type, or the method of attack. The company said 1 crew member is missing, 11 are injured and receiving medical care where required, and the rest of the crew have been evacuated from the vessel.
“Our immediate priority is supporting the search and rescue effort, our crew and those affected,” ADNOC L&S said, as reported by Gulf News on 18 November. The company “reiterates the importance of protecting seafarers and safeguarding freedom of navigation and maritime security,” according to The National.
ADNOC did not disclose crew nationalities, the vessel’s destination, its cargo, or whether the vessel remained afloat. No UKMTO advisory number specifically covering the ADNOC vessel has been confirmed.
Reuters, citing anonymous maritime security sources, reported separately that a liquefied petroleum gas tanker was struck by a projectile while transiting the strait and that the crew abandoned ship, according to a report published via Yahoo News on 18 November. Reuters did not confirm whether this was the same vessel ADNOC described. The 2 reports overlap in timing and location, but no official source has linked them. ADNOC’s deliberate withholding of the vessel’s type and cargo makes it impossible to determine from public information alone whether its vessel was the LPG tanker Reuters sources described.
The Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT Tara Gas was struck near Khasab, Oman, with the first attack reported at approximately 1900 UTC on 16 November 2026, according to gCaptain and India’s Ministry of External Affairs. This is a separate incident from the ADNOC attack.
MT Tara Gas was struck a second time on 17 November, causing a further fire and disabling the vessel, gCaptain reported. India’s Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that 21 Indian nationals were evacuated to Khasab, with 2 hospitalised and 1 Indian national missing. The vessel carried a total crew of 25, of whom 24 were Indian nationals, according to The Daily Jagran.
“We condemn the attack on the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT TARA GAS in the Strait of Hormuz on 16 November 2026,” India’s Ministry of External Affairs said in its statement, as reported by The Daily Jagran.
Tara Gas is owned by Global Gas Inc and managed by UAE-based Matrix Maritime Solutions FZE, according to Reuters and Riviera Maritime. The vessel has no connection to ADNOC.
UKMTO Warning 208-26 covers the Tara Gas incident north of Khasab. A separate advisory, UKMTO Warning 207-26, covers the Panama-flagged crude tanker On Phoenix, also struck by an unknown projectile on 16 November and UAE-owned, according to gCaptain. The On Phoenix crew status has not been publicly reported. The Iran Navy had confirmed a 4th tanker hit in Hormuz near Khasab days before the Tara Gas attack, part of a sustained surge of violence near the tip of Oman’s Musandam Peninsula.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and navy said on 17 November that a ship carrying LNG and 2 oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, without naming specific vessels or operators, according to Reuters. Reuters said it could not independently verify this claim. The IRGC’s reference to an LNG carrier and 2 oil tankers does not precisely match the known incidents — Tara Gas carried LPG, not LNG, the On Phoenix is a crude tanker, and the ADNOC vessel’s type remains undisclosed. No IRNA, PressTV, or Tasnim article specifically claiming or denying responsibility for the ADNOC attack had been published as of 18 November.
The IRGC has consistently framed tanker casualties as vessels hitting naval mines after operating on “unauthorized southern routes,” according to Riviera Maritime. No independent investigation has resolved the competing accounts of how vessels in the strait are being struck.
The 16–17 November attacks came as the Araghchi-Busaidi talks in Muscat on 17 November produced no Hormuz agreement , and as broader US-Iran peace talks remained stalled with no sign of a breakthrough on the strait.
By August 2026, ADNOC L&S had confirmed that 15 of its vessels were attacked by missiles and drones in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, killing 1 crew member and injuring 20, according to The National and the Shipping Telegraph. The 17 November attack — with 1 missing and 11 injured — produced more injuries in a single incident than half that prior cumulative total.
The August attacks escalated sharply, with ADNOC confirming multiple vessels hit in rapid succession, according to The National. A separate ADNOC L&S vessel was damaged in an attack in UAE territorial waters on 10 November 2026, according to gCaptain. ADNOC L&S manages a fleet of 500 to 800 active vessels, including owned and chartered tonnage, making its operations a persistent target across the waterway.
The UAE Foreign Ministry said in August 2026 that Iran’s attacks on ADNOC vessels constituted “a flagrant violation” of UN Security Council Resolution 2817 and described the targeting of commercial shipping as an “act of piracy by the IRGC,” according to Al Jazeera.
Dr Anwar Gargash, Diplomatic Adviser to the UAE President, said after a further ADNOC vessel attack on 14 August that repeated strikes “would not change the UAE’s approach of deterrence, diplomacy and adherence to international law,” Reuters reported.
No UAE government statement specifically addressing the 17 November attack had been issued as of 18 November.
The Joint Maritime Information Center maintained the threat level for the Strait of Hormuz at SEVERE as of its latest advisory in early November, warning that deliberate attacks are “highly likely,” according to JMIC. Transit volumes, which JMIC has described as “single-digit to low-double-digit” per day, remain far below the pre-war baseline of 130 to 140 daily transits reported by Reuters.
The following table summarises the 3 vessel incidents from 16–17 November alone:
Iran first closed the Strait of Hormuz on 28 February 2026 alongside the opening of hostilities. After a ceasefire reopening, Iran re-closed the strait on 18 April. The IRGC redeclared the closure in July.
The attacks on 16–17 November followed the IRGC claim on 15 November that a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels sank in the Gulf , and coincided with US strikes on Qeshm Island in the strait itself.
India’s condemnation of the Tara Gas attack added another government to the roster of states directly protesting Iran’s actions in the waterway. India had previously condemned attacks on the VLCC MT Fujairah Energy in the Persian Gulf , also involving Indian crew members.
